description: US/CA-only refactor deny-list (docs/refactor-plan.md Phase 10): removed markets, data sources, and symbols that must not reappear in shipped code. Matched case-insensitively as substrings, scoped to agent/src, agent/backtest, and frontend/src. Intentional mentions belong in `allow` below, each with a non-empty reason; an allow entry suppresses exactly the listed tokens for the matching path (repo-relative path or fnmatch glob). agent/tests/test_us_ca_scope_gate.py enforces both the deny-list and the allowlist's honesty (every entry must carry a reason and must still suppress a real hit). Phase 11 token-spelling note: the matcher is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING search, so short exchange suffixes and currency codes cannot be added bare. Measured collisions in the scan roots at Phase 11: nse 2131 hits (response/sense/expense), bse 1088, hose 533 (those/whose/chose), lse 4987 (false/else/pulse), .BO 127 (".bold"/".bootstrap"/".body"), .BA 473 (".back"/".base"), .SS 25 (".ssl"/".sse"), .SH 398 (".sh"/".sha256"), .L 2665, ARS 2794 (years/args), and HKD/CNY/GBP/INR/JPY/KRW/VND all collide with the surviving multi-currency portfolio/FX tables (portfolio/service.py, portfolio/iso4217.py, market_data.py). Those bare forms are therefore omitted. Exchange suffixes are an exception: in code a suffix can only be a string literal (a comment cannot route a market), so the suffix tokens below carry their CLOSING double quote - '.SS"' matches ".SS" in a suffix table, endswith(".SS") and f"{code}.SS", but never '.ssl'/'.sse'. '.SH"' is the one suffix that still collides (file-extension lists like ".sh") and '.HK"' still matches surviving portfolio HK-journal handling, so both are omitted and the exact symbols stay as guards. crypto/forex/futures stay untokened for the same reason: crypto is a surviving Robinhood instrument class and MARKET_SPECS market, while forex/futures appear in generic prose and surviving symbol classification. Longer multi-word venue names (hong kong, shanghai, shenzhen, buenos aires) plus kospi/kosdaq are specific enough to include; their surviving prose mentions are allowlisted below. Phase 13 token-spelling note: two spellings that Phase 10/11 missed because they are neither the internal market id nor a denylisted token are now covered. 'china_a' is the hyphen-free internal market id the shadow-account skill still used in prose; it has exactly one hit in the scan roots (agent/src/skills/shadow-account/SKILL.md) and that line was corrected to us/ca rather than allowlisted, so the token carries no allow entry. 'a-share' is the human spelling; adding it is a deliberate exception to the 'prose collisions stay un-tokened' rule above, because the failure it catches is precisely a PROMPT surface (a bundled skill or context file naming a removed market), which no other token covers. Measured at Phase 13: 16 hits across 13 files, with zero substring collisions (checked against data-shared / meta-share / beta-share / delta-share / alpha-share / extra-shared and the [a-z]a-share shape). Every one of those 13 files uses the term only in explanatory prose about the removal itself, or in research_papers_tool's intentional topic regex, so each is allowlisted individually with its own reason rather than left as a blind spot.
